svg.style: display: block; width: 100%; height: auto; font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif; background: rgb(247, 244, 236);
svg.title: Analytics Engineering — XKCD and Jaffle Shop full architecture, version 5
svg.desc: Two sources feed a shared MotherDuck warehouse: XKCD through Dagster and Cloudflare R2, and Jaffle Shop CSVs through dbt seed. dbt produces marts in MotherDuck. Logical Comics and Jaffle USS datamarts group those tables without copying data. Comics links to calendar with no bridge; cafe_bridge points to six Jaffle tables. Malloy adds dimensions, measures and join relationships. Its packages serve Credible AI chat and Malloy Publisher Explorer and MCP, with external MCP agents. A planned comics trend agent has an undecided Publisher or direct MotherDuck route. The lower lanes show Cloud Run runtime, Scheduler, secrets, SQLite backups, monitoring, automated Dagster deployment and automated semantic deployment.
svg.text: Two domains. Shared platform. Reusable analytic modules.
Dashed gold = planned alternatives, not deployed connections

g.text: One container · min 0 / max 1 · scales to zero · restores state before starting
Control paths and state protection · not additional data sources
Both release paths automated. One-time bootstrap and break-glass script remain manual.

svg.text: No copies or separate databases; not tenant security isolation.
Source models are versioned in GitHub.
Shared tables; logical domain groupings only.
Logical ingestion and transformation steps above execute in the deployed runtime below.

g.text: Candidate B · direct MotherDuck · decision pending

g.title: Comics datamart: Logical domain abstraction over data_warehouse_demo.marts.comics and calendar in the shared MotherDuck warehouse. Comics links to calendar using Calendar_key = _key_calendar; there is no bridge table. The topology is shown here; Malloy defines the join relationship, dimensions and measures in the next stage. No data copies, separate databases or tenant security boundaries are implied.

Jaffle Shop datamart: Logical Unified Star Schema (USS) over seven data_warehouse_demo.marts tables, all within MotherDuck. cafe_bridge is the single entry point and points to cafe_customers, cafe_locations, cafe_orders, cafe_order_items, cafe_products and cafe_supplies through six _Key_cafe_* columns. Malloy defines six join_one relationships and entity dimensions/measures, exposing cafe_bridge_explore. Pick one Stage per query or use the stage-filter pattern to prevent NULL keys from excluding another stage. This is logical domain isolation, not a physical database split or a security boundary.

g.text: All seven tables remain in MotherDuck marts.

g.title: Comics: One of exactly two input sources. Dagster reads the latest comic ID, fetches only missing JSON documents in a 20-worker pool, and skips comic #404. Full refresh is optional.
Jaffle Shop: The second input source is the six committed Jaffle Shop CSV files. It is not a live commerce connector and does not pass through the R2 JSON landing zone.

Dagster fetch: The raw_comics asset downloads missing comics and writes one raw_comics/{num}.json document per comic to Cloudflare R2. This card depicts a logical step executed inside the Dagster runtime below.

Dagster load: The raw_comics_v2 asset reads missing JSON files from R2, validates the records against the schema configuration, and loads queryable rows to MotherDuck. Its materialization triggers the comics transformation sensor.

dbt seed: Dagster runs the six dbt seed assets sequentially. The last seed, raw_supplies, triggers jaffle_shop_transformation_job through an asset sensor. The repository describes this ingestion as a manual/local run, not the monthly comics Scheduler job.
Cloudflare R2: R2 holds raw comic files, not queryable warehouse tables. The raw data zone and the Dagster SQLite backup zone use two prefixes within one R2 bucket.
dbt build + test: Dagster invokes dbt at runtime; SQL transformations and data tests execute against MotherDuck. dbt docs generation is separate and occurs at image-build time.

MotherDuck: Both domains share data_warehouse_demo. MotherDuck stores raw, staging, intermediate and mart tables and executes dbt SQL. XKCD uses int_comics. Jaffle Shop now has seven int_cafe_* models and seven cafe_* marts, including cafe_bridge. The semantic packages read only marts, not staging or intermediate.

comics: The comics Malloy package maps MotherDuck marts, refines dimensions/measures and joins, and exposes comics_explore. It is versioned in this repo and published to Credible. The Publisher deployment copies the canonical package into its build context.

jaffle_shop: The Jaffle Shop Malloy package reads seven cafe_* marts including cafe_bridge. Six entity refinements define keys, dimensions and measures; a bridge refinement joins them into cafe_bridge_explore. Credible and Publisher serve the same canonical package. The package does not read intermediate tables.

Credible: Credible consumes the two published semantic packages. AI chat for exploration is included explicitly from your clarification. The publishing pipeline versions packages before publishing them to Credible.

Malloy Publisher: The self-hosted Publisher serves the two packages with Explorer and MCP access. It is deployed as malloy-publisher-mcp in a separate Cloud Run service, using the analytics-malloy-publisher-rag repository as its build context. This diagram represents reads/serving relationships, not copies of warehouse data.
AI agents: External AI agents can consume the Malloy Publisher MCP tool surface. These clients are distinct from the future comics trend-analysis agent.

Comics trend agent: The comics trend-analysis agent is a roadmap entity, not implemented. You have not decided whether it reads through Malloy Publisher or directly queries MotherDuck. Both dotted candidate connections are alternatives, not two implemented dependencies.

nginx: nginx routes public requests to Dagster UI/GraphQL, static dbt docs, and the wake API. Cloud Run terminates TLS; nginx listens on the container's public port. Low-idle-cost design — Single-container packaging. nginx multiplexes wake, Dagster UI/GraphQL and static docs on one public port. Not inherently required by scale-to-zero. Separate services or another ingress/router could replace it; UI/docs routing still needs a home.

wake API: The Starlette/uvicorn wake service authenticates the X-Wake-Secret header, launches comics ingestion idempotently via Dagster GraphQL, waits for the sensor-triggered transformation, and returns the run result. Low-idle-cost design — External wake + control. With a continuously running Dagster daemon, enable its native schedule and remove this custom HTTP launch/wait bridge if no other clients need it. Authenticated triggering and run monitoring still need coverage.

Dagster runtime: Dagster executes the ingestion assets and dbt assets, exposes its UI and GraphQL API, and persists run/schedule state in SQLite. Two sensors trigger domain transformations. The in-code comics schedule is forced STOPPED; Cloud Scheduler is the monthly trigger.
dbt runtime: dbt project code is packaged into the image. dbt transformations and tests execute only when Dagster launches the assets; they do not execute during the container image build.
dbt docs: dbt deps and dbt docs generate run at image-build time. nginx serves the generated static documentation at /dbt-docs/, so cold starts do not need to query MotherDuck for docs metadata.

Dagster SQLite: SQLite stores Dagster run history, event logs, and schedule state. It is ephemeral inside the Cloud Run container unless protected by Litestream's R2 replicas and cold-start restore. Low-idle-cost design — Ephemeral-state protection. Local SQLite is ephemeral on Cloud Run, even with minimum instances above zero. Durable external Dagster storage could replace the local SQLite + replica/restore pattern.

Litestream: Litestream replicates SQLite into the epoch-based dagster_home/ backup zone. Startup restores and quick-checks databases before Dagster starts. By default corrupted databases are quarantined and recreated in a new replica epoch; undecodable content is reset. Other restore failures still abort startup. DAGSTER_RESTORE_SELF_HEAL=0 restores strict fail-fast behavior. This recovery may lose affected local history; MotherDuck data is separate. Low-idle-cost design — Ephemeral-state protection. Replicate and restore is necessary for this local-SQLite design across instance loss. External persistent Dagster storage could remove these scripts; an always-on service alone cannot.

supervisord: The supervisor configuration manages nginx, wake API, Dagster and Litestream. The entrypoint restores state, forces the in-code monthly schedule stopped, and renders nginx before starting supervisor. Low-idle-cost design — Single-container packaging. Single-container process management is packaging overhead, not a scale-to-zero requirement. Separate managed services could replace supervisord; process lifecycle management is still needed.

Cloud Scheduler: Two HTTP Scheduler jobs wake and check the comics pipeline. They call nginx's wake routes; the wake service uses Dagster GraphQL to start and monitor the runs. Jaffle ingestion is manual/local. Low-idle-cost design — External wake + control. An always-on Dagster scheduler or another external orchestrator could replace these monthly HTTP wake/status jobs. Scheduling, retries and missed-run detection still matter.

Secret Manager: One-time bootstrap creates the wake secret and grants IAM. MotherDuck and R2 secrets must already be populated. Cloud Build uses the MotherDuck token for docs; Cloud Run receives references to runtime secrets. Secrets are not baked into the image.
Cloud Logging: Runtime logs and failure events are collected by Cloud Logging. Bootstrap creates log-based failure metrics used by Monitoring alert policies.

Cloudflare R2: A distinct logical prefix in the same R2 bucket stores Dagster state. _epoch.json points at the active generation; _quarantine/ preserves corrupt database copies, and older epochs remain archived. This is not a third data source or a warehouse table backup. Low-idle-cost design — Ephemeral-state protection. The dagster_home/ replica prefix can be retired if Dagster state moves to durable external storage with its own backup policy. This does not remove the raw_comics/ landing zone or the need for backups.

Reviewer / analyst: A browser connects through nginx to the Dagster UI and static dbt docs. Direct SQL inspection of MotherDuck is also possible; the primary analytic consumption surfaces are shown in the top data plane.
Cloud Monitoring: Monitoring watches the configured failure metrics and alert policies. A second Scheduler status check acts as a dead-man's-switch for the monthly pipeline.
Email alerts: Configured notification channels deliver failure alerts to the configured email address. This is operational monitoring, not an analytic data consumer.

GitHub repository: Source control for Dagster, dbt, seeds, Malloy and image/release definitions. Relevant pushes to main trigger Deploy Dagster. Semantic workspace pushes separately bump and publish packages, then deploy Publisher. Both deployments now run through GitHub Actions.

GitHub Actions: deploy-dagster.yml validates relevant PRs without deploying. Relevant pushes to main, or workflow_dispatch, validate definitions and parse dbt, use keyless GCP workload identity, check the monthly blackout and active runs, then invoke deploy_dagster.sh. It serializes releases, tags the checked-out commit, and asserts the live image, traffic and endpoints. The script remains a manual break-glass route, bypassing workflow validation and live-run guards.

Cloud Build + Docker: Cloud Build runs the Dockerfile with BuildKit, installs dependencies, packages Dagster/dbt source, and generates static dbt docs using the build secret. Docker is build tooling, not a separate runtime service.

Container Registry: The tagged image is pushed to the gcr.io registry address by Cloud Build. GitHub Actions derives an immutable sha-<commit> tag and the shared release script deploys that image to Cloud Run.

Dagster on Cloud Run: GitHub Actions invokes deploy_dagster.sh to build/deploy analytics-dagster, upsert both Scheduler jobs, route traffic to the latest revision and verify readiness. The workflow additionally asserts the image tag and endpoints. min instances 0, max 1; CPU remains allocated while an instance exists. The same script is the break-glass fallback. Low-idle-cost design — Min-zero policy. Min 0 / max 1 trades idle instance cost for cold starts. Min 1 with a continuously running daemon could simplify wake-up logic, but does not guarantee local state persistence. Active compute, storage and other services still cost money.

GCP bootstrap (once): A developer runs scripts/bootstrap_gcp.sh once to enable APIs, grant IAM, create the wake shared secret and set up alert metrics/channels/policies. MotherDuck and R2 secrets must be supplied separately. Bootstrap remains manual; routine Dagster and Publisher deployment is automated.

GitHub Actions: Pushes to semantic_layer/workspace/** on main trigger changed-package version bumps, then the reusable Credible publishing workflow. Version bumps are committed with skip-ci protection.
Credible publish: Credible packages are published by CI/CD, not manually from a laptop. A successful Bump and Publish Packages workflow triggers Deploy Publisher.

Publisher image build: The workflow checks out analytics-malloy-publisher-rag, copies the canonical Malloy packages into that build context, and submits it to Cloud Build. It builds a separate Publisher image tagged with the canonical repository commit.

Publisher on Cloud Run: The Publisher service uses a separate Cloud Run deployment with its MotherDuck secret. CI routes traffic to the new revision and checks the status endpoint for serving state and both packages. Low-idle-cost design — Min-zero policy. The independent Publisher service also has min 0, so on-demand requests can incur cold starts. Min 1 reduces that trade-off at an idle-instance cost; it does not require the Dagster wake API.

g.text: MONTHLY RUN · FOLLOW THE NUMBERED CONTROL ARROWS
Cold-start restore precedes request handling. 12:00 status check repeats routes 1–3 without launching new work. Backups, UI routes and monitoring are parallel, not numbered steps.
Required here ≠ universally required · security, monitoring and backups still matter
Dagster and Publisher scale down when idle.
Lower idle compute, with cold-start latency.
Not a promise of zero total platform cost.
A request can start a zero-instance service.
Always-on: native Dagster schedule can replace
this bridge; keep retries and missed-run checks.
Restore + integrity check; quarantine corrupt state.
Min 1 alone does NOT make local state persistent.
nginx routes wake, UI/GraphQL and dbt docs.
